rule: one JSON array is a review verdict, including non-empty findings; a whole-message (none) is the low-level protocol's clean verdict; every other non-empty shape is UNPARSEABLE and attests verdict=fail output_contract=prose_unparseable; only an empty message stays silent
context: every payload is delivered as a SubagentStop under a forked-skill marker sidecar (forkedSkill true, skillName code-review); only the text varies

suffixes..attest: a row is written and the verdict is derived from the blocking count
suffixes..unparseable: a row is written carrying verdict=fail and output_contract=prose_unparseable
suffixes..silent: no row is written and the classifier never runs

shapes.headered-json-clean.attest: the two live self-review shapes: header, empty fence, closing sentence
shapes.bare-fence-clean.attest: a fork ending in a fenced empty array with no header
shapes.fence-nonempty.attest: one valid findings array is a failed review verdict
shapes.none-buried-in-prose.unparseable: the marker inside longer output is not the marker, so it is not a clean verdict; it is also not silence
shapes.none-after-failure-note.unparseable: an excuse line above the marker: the reviewer said it could not inspect the diff, which is the shape that must never read as clean
shapes.live-specimen-scope-note.unparseable: measured live 2026-08: marker, blank line, scope sentence naming the excluded file, em dash byte-exact
shapes.later-fence-carries-findings.unparseable: two fences disagree, so the hook cannot tell which is the verdict
shapes.findings-then-exclusion-fence.unparseabl: real findings first, later empty exclusion fence: same ambiguity, opposite order
shapes.unparseable-prose.unparseable: no verdict shape at all - the case x-c446 was filed for
shapes.empty-message.silent: no message: the fork said nothing, which is a different condition from saying something unreadable

why_unparseable_is_not_silent: x-c446. A review that ran and answered unreadably used to leave no row, which is byte-identical at the gate to a review that never ran. Four mechanisms read that row and all read zero. The unparseable rows below now attest verdict=fail, so the round is counted and the PR is not cleared; they never attest a pass, so nothing is cleared on evidence that did not arrive.
byte_exactness_note: The payloads are RECORDED data, not authored prose: they reproduce the fork's final text byte for byte, and live-specimen-scope-note.unparseable deliberately carries a real U+2014 em dash in a tracked file under the recorded-data exemption to the no-em-dash authoring rule. Rewriting it as a hyphen is the exact drift (green on the wrong bytes) this corpus exists to catch.
